_about: AI-assisted: researched and assembled with ChatGPT (OpenAI). See docs/AI_USAGE.md. Snapshot compiled 2026-09-26 from cited public records. Statuses and roles are time-bound to source dates; charges are allegations, and reported deaths are not convictions. Public senior figures only; country-level geographic associations; no operational routes, enforcement weaknesses, or unlicensed photos.

sources.title: Treasury Announces Sanctions of Mexican Drug Lords
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of the Treasury
sources.claim: Treasury identifies the Gulf Cartel as a Mexico-based drug trafficking organization and names senior figures.

sources.title: Head of the Gulf Cartel indicted
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Southern District of Texas
sources.claim: DOJ identifies Cartel del Golfo, also called the Gulf Cartel or CDG, as the organization in the indictment.

people.name: Juan García Ábrego
people.roleLabel: Former Gulf Cartel leader; sentenced to life in U.S. federal court

sources.title: Audit Report 97-29A
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Inspector General
sources.claim: DOJ OIG reports García Ábrego was convicted on 22 counts and sentenced in January 1997 to multiple life terms.

sources.title: Mexico’s Drug Trafficking Organizations: Source and Scope of the Rising Violence
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice
sources.claim: DOJ-hosted history identifies García Ábrego as the Gulf organization’s leader in the 1980s and Osiel Cárdenas Guillén as his successor.

people.name: Osiel Cárdenas Guillén
people.roleLabel: Former Gulf Cartel leader; convicted of drug and related offenses

sources.title: Osiel Cardenas-Guillen, Former Head of the Gulf Cartel, Sentenced to 25 Years Imprisonment
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Southern District of Texas
sources.claim: DOJ reports Cárdenas Guillén pleaded guilty and was sentenced to 25 years for drug trafficking, money laundering, and threats to federal agents.

sources.title: Mexico’s Drug Trafficking Organizations: Source and Scope of the Rising Violence

people.name: Antonio Ezequiel Cárdenas Guillén
people.roleLabel: Gulf Cartel leader reported killed in 2010

sources.title: Comunicado de Prensa 300/2010
sources.publisher: Secretaría de Marina-Armada de México
sources.claim: Mexico’s Navy reports that Antonio Ezequiel Cárdenas Guillén, alias Tony Tormenta, was a Gulf Cartel leader killed on 5 November 2010.

sources.title: Treasury Announces Sanctions of Mexican Drug Lords
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of the Treasury

people.name: Jorge Eduardo Costilla Sánchez
people.roleLabel: Former Gulf Cartel leader; sentenced to life in U.S. federal court

sources.title: Former head of Gulf Cartel receives life sentence for importing kilos of drugs
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Southern District of Texas
sources.claim: DOJ reports Costilla Sánchez pleaded guilty to cocaine and marijuana trafficking and received a life sentence; it identifies him as cartel head after Osiel Cárdenas Guillén’s arrest.

sources.title: Treasury Announces Sanctions of Mexican Drug Lords
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of the Treasury
sources.claim: Treasury names Costilla Sánchez and Antonio Ezequiel Cárdenas Guillén together as directors of Gulf Cartel trafficking in 2009.

people.name: Mario Cárdenas Guillén

sources.title: Comunicado de Prensa 181/2012

sources.title: FY14 Reviews of the DOJ Annual Accounting of Drug Control Funds and Related Performance
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Inspector General
